prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: sideswipe while changing lanes in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a passenger and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1205; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the right lane of a Baytown, Texas roadway when Driver 1 signaled and began moving left to change lanes. Driver 2, operating a vehicle in the adjacent left lane, moved into the same space at roughly the same time, and the two vehicles sideswiped one another. Driver 1 stated that the contact was sudden and that Driver 1 was unable to avoid it. Driver 2 gave a statement consistent with that account, and two independent witnesses at the scene described the lane change and the contact in the same way. Photographs taken at the scene show damage along the left side of Driver 1's vehicle and matching scraping on the right side of Driver 2's vehicle, which is consistent with the reported impact. Driver 1 is the named insured on the policy covering the vehicle. Passenger was seated in the front passenger position and reported pain in the right knee after the collision. Responding officers confirmed Passenger's presence in the vehicle at the time of the crash. No prior damage to the vehicle was reported or observed during the inspection. Passenger was transported for evaluation, and the reported knee injury is a plausible result of the forces involved in this type of collision.
